title: Conjunctions & Interjections
description: Learn conjunctions and interjections for Grade 6: coordinating (FANBOYS), subordinating and correlative conjunctions, plus interjections and their punctuation — with practice and tests.

topics.title: Coordinating, Subordinating & Correlative Conjunctions
topics.concept:
Coordinating conjunctions join two equal items — two words, two phrases or two independent clauses. Remember them as FANBOYS: for, and, nor, but, or, yet, so.

  • Tea or coffee? (two words)
  • She studied hard, so she passed. (two clauses)

Subordinating conjunctions join a dependent clause to a main clause and show a relationship — reason, time, condition, contrast: because, since, as, when, while, after, before, if, unless, although, though.

  • Although it rained, we played.

Correlative conjunctions come in pairs: either…or, neither…nor, both…and, not only…but also, whether…or.

  • Both Ravi and Sita came.

examples.problem: Join with a conjunction: He is poor. He is honest.
examples.solution: He is poor but honest. — 'but' shows a contrast between the two ideas.

examples.problem: Complete the correlative pair: ___ Ravi ___ Sam was present; the room was empty.
examples.solution: Neither … nor — 'Neither Ravi nor Sam was present' fits the empty-room meaning.

recap: Subordinating join a dependent clause and show reason/time/condition/contrast
Correlative conjunctions always come in pairs

topics.title: Interjections & Their Punctuation
topics.concept:
An interjection is a word or short phrase that expresses sudden emotion. It is grammatically separate from the rest of the sentence.

FeelingInterjections
JoyHurray! Yippee! Wow!
SurpriseOh! What! Really!
Sorrow / pityAlas! Oh no!
DisgustUgh! Yuck!
ApprovalBravo! Well done!

Punctuation: a strong interjection takes an exclamation mark (Wow!); a mild one takes a comma (Well, let me think).

examples.solution: Alas! He failed the test. — 'Alas' expresses sorrow and takes an exclamation mark.

examples.problem: Which interjection shows joy? Ugh / Hurray / Alas

recap: Interjections express sudden feeling and stand apart

options: Because he is rich, so he is proud.
Because he is rich, he is proud.
He is proud because so rich.
So he is rich because proud.

questions.q: 'Hurry up ___ you will miss the train.'
Identify the correlative pair: 'Either you apologise ___ you leave.'
Spot the error: 'Though he is talented yet he is lazy.'
questions.explanation: 'Though' and 'yet' should not be used together.

questions.q: Choose the parallel structure: 'She is not only intelligent ___.'
questions.explanation: 'not only … but also' keeps parallel adjectives: intelligent … hardworking.

questions.q: Fill in correctly: 'Scarcely had I sat down ___ the phone rang.'

options: No sooner I reached than it rained.
No sooner did I reach than it rained.
No sooner I reached then it rained.
No sooner reached I when it rained.
questions.explanation: 'No sooner did I reach than …' uses inversion.

questions.q: Identify the error: 'Neither of the answers are correct.'
Choose: 'He worked hard ___ he could clear the exam.'
Rearrange: 'also / not / he / only / sang / but / danced'
options: He not only sang but also danced.
Not only he sang but danced also.
He sang not only danced but also.
Only not he sang but also danced.
questions.explanation: 'He not only sang but also danced.' is correct and parallel.

questions.q: Which option correctly combines: 'He is honest. He is hardworking.' (correlative)
options: He is both honest and hardworking.
questions.explanation: 'both … and' joins the two equal qualities.

outcomes: Define conjunctions and use them to join words and sentences

intro.en: A conjunction is a joining word — it links words, phrases or sentences. An interjection is a short word that suddenly expresses feeling. In "Hurray! We won because we practised hard and stayed calm," Hurray is an interjection while because and and are conjunctions.
intro.hi: समुच्चयबोधक (Conjunction) जोड़ने वाला शब्द है — यह शब्दों, वाक्यांशों या वाक्यों को जोड़ता है। विस्मयादिबोधक (Interjection) भावना अचानक प्रकट करने वाला शब्द है। "Hurray! We won because we practised hard and stayed calm" में Hurray विस्मयादिबोधक है, और because, and समुच्चयबोधक हैं।

real_life.situation:
Your friend shares news:

Friend: Wow! I got the scholarship because I worked hard, but I still need to fill the form and submit it today.
real_life.why: Wow bursts out a feeling (interjection). Because, but, and stitch the ideas together (conjunctions). Together they make speech sound natural and connected.

rule_box.formula: FANBOYS = For, And, Nor, But, Or, Yet, So
rule_box.example: I was tired, so I rested; but I finished the work because it was urgent.

quick_test.explanation: and, but, or, so are coordinating conjunctions (part of FANBOYS).

common_mistakes.wrong: Although he is rich, but he is unhappy.
common_mistakes.right: Although he is rich, he is unhappy.
common_mistakes.note: Don't use 'although' and 'but' together; one is enough.

common_mistakes.wrong: Because he was ill, so he stayed home.
common_mistakes.right: Because he was ill, he stayed home.

common_mistakes.note: A strong interjection needs an exclamation mark.

fill_l1.instructions: Fill in a suitable coordinating conjunction (and, but, or, so).

items.q: Hurry up ______ you will miss the bus.
It was raining, ______ we stayed inside.

fill_l2.instructions: Fill in a subordinating or correlative conjunction.

items.q: ______ it was late, we continued working. (contrast)
I will call you ______ I reach home. (time)
______ you study, you will fail. (condition – if not)
He stayed home ______ he was unwell. (reason)

error_detection.sentence: Although she tried, but she lost.
Because it rained, so we cancelled the trip.
error_detection.correct: Because it rained, we cancelled the trip.

error_detection.sentence: Either he nor his brother came.
error_detection.correct: Either he or his brother came.

sentence_correction.wrong: Though he is poor but he is honest.
sentence_correction.correct: Though he is poor, he is honest.

sentence_correction.wrong: Neither the boys or the girls were ready.
sentence_correction.correct: Neither the boys nor the girls were ready.

rearrangement.jumbled: because / late / he / was / he / ran
rearrangement.answer: He ran because he was late.

reading.passage: Wow! The school fair was wonderful. Both the dance and the drama were excellent, although the food stall ran out of samosas. "Alas!" cried Sam, "I came late, so I missed the magic show." Still, neither the heat nor the crowd could spoil the fun.

questions.q: Pick out one interjection from the passage.
Find a correlative pair of conjunctions.

questions.answer: although — it contrasts the good fair with the food running out.

speaking: Hurry up, or we will be late.
Although it was cold, we went out.
Neither he nor she was present.
Wow! That was an amazing goal!

writing.prompt: Write five sentences about a school event, using and, but, because, a correlative pair, and one interjection.
writing.example: Hurray! We won the quiz. Both teams played well, but we scored more because we stayed calm.

options: Although he tried but he failed.

micro_quiz.q: '___! We lost the match.' Which interjection of sorrow fits?

challenge.q: Identify the error: 'No sooner he arrived than the bell rang.'
options: No sooner he arrived → No sooner did he arrive
challenge.explanation: After 'No sooner', use inversion: 'No sooner did he arrive than …'.

options: Not only he sings but dances.
He not only sings but also dances.
He sings not only but dances also.
Not only sings he but dance.
challenge.explanation: 'not only … but also' must keep parallel verbs: sings … dances.

options: Well I think we should go.
Well, I think we should go.
Well! I think we should go.
Well; I think we should go.
challenge.explanation: A mild interjection 'Well' takes a comma.

Subordinating join a dependent clause (because, although, when, if)
Correlative come in pairs (either…or, neither…nor, both…and)
